description: Build an autocomplete tool that returns the three most frequent stored sentences matching the text typed so far, breaking equal-frequency ties alphabetically. Typing # saves the current text as a sentence and clears the query. Example 1: with "i love you" occurring 5 times, "island" 3 times, and "i love leetcode" 2 times, typing i returns those three in that order. Example 2: then typing a space returns ["i love you", "i love leetcode"]. Constraints: input characters are lowercase letters, spaces, or #; stored counts and sentence lengths fit in memory.
intuition: Store sentence candidates at every prefix so a query only sorts sentences that match the typed prefix.

brute_force.approach: Scan every sentence, filter by prefix, and sort all matches for each typed character.
brute_force.time: input O(S log S), initialization O(S)

optimal.approach: Map each prefix to its matching sentences and rank only that prefix's candidates by frequency and lexical order.
optimal.time: input O(P log P), initialization O(total sentence characters)

edge_cases: Typing # commits the sentence and returns an empty suggestion list.
A prefix with no stored matches returns an empty list.
